paths.description: Unauthenticated overview marketing template and primary account entry; tested desktop, mobile, dark, increased contrast, reduced motion, network, performance, no-JS and memory conditions.
Passkey education/detail template and Create a passkey action.
Sign in with Google detail template and account connection actions.
Google Account authentication entry through the labelled identifier step; no credentials submitted.

findings.summary: The public Google Account pages do not honor the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot remains white and computed color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens, preserving brand contrast.

findings.summary: The fixed cookie notice obscures a substantial part of the mobile hero.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, the notice covers roughly the bottom 194px and overlaps hero copy until accepted.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-overlapping consent treatment with a clear choice and persist the decision; avoid covering primary content.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.9s, TBT 850ms, CLS 0.175 and performance 0.40; desktop trace LCP was 1.90s, showing condition sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, reduce startup JavaScript and animation work, and defer non-critical third-party/decorative resources.

findings.summary: The mobile page shifts visibly after initial layout.
findings.evidence: CDP layout observer recorded CLS 0.1493 at 4.44s; Lighthouse recorded CLS 0.175.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the late shifting element, reserve its final space, and use metric-compatible font fallbacks and stable consent placement.

findings.summary: The content-light landing page ships an excessive request, font, fetch, and decorative-animation payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 295 requests/3.39MB, including 24 fonts/994KB, 43 fetches/1.86MB, 204 image/Lottie requests and six render-blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and consolidate fonts, defer below-fold Lottie/assets, remove unused bundles, and ensure only true critical resources block rendering.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated account landing page loads a large analytics and cross-origin footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker inventory found Tag Manager and Analytics; HAR classed 102 requests/3.38MB as third-party relative to myaccount.google.com, and a Google cookie lasts 396 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize pre-consent analytics and cross-origin requests, shorten non-essential retention, and load analytics only after an applicable consent signal.

findings.summary: Several baseline browser-enforced response defenses are absent on the inspected final page.
findings.evidence: Header audit found no CSP, HSTS, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; nosniff was present and the cookie was Secure/HttpOnly/Lax.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy on the final marketing response.

findings.summary: The non-JavaScript crawler path is rate-limited and does not expose the intended marketing content.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetch returned HTTP 429, only 12% rendered-word overlap, and no matching raw title/H1/description; Lighthouse’s browser SEO score was 0.92.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve stable semantic HTML and metadata to legitimate non-JS crawlers, and return an actionable Retry-After/recovery response when rate limiting is necessary.

findings.summary: The static marketing page starts with a disproportionately large object and graphics footprint.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary measured 539,263 nodes and 25.56MB self size, including about 17.5k Float32Arrays and ArrayBuffers, consistent with many Lottie assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Instantiate decorative animations only near the viewport, release animation buffers after completion, and prefer static assets where motion adds little value.
